lead.label: 3d
lead.why: Abstract: 'Compounds 3d (84.09%), 3g, and 3a demonstrated significant anti-inflammatory activity'; results: 3d 'most potent inhibitor of the series' (COX-2 IC50 0.06 uM) and 'most promising analog'; conclusion: 'compound 3d as the most potent compound of the series'.

reactions.conditions: Equimolar mixture heated in polyphosphoric acid (PPA, 24 g) at 80-95 C for 5-6 h; poured on ice water, neutralised with 10 N NaOH, extracted with toluene, recrystallised from EtOH; 84%.

General procedure 4.1.3: acid (0.02 mol), DCC (0.01 mol), CH2Cl2 (50 mL), rt 3-4 h; filter off dicyclohexylurea, evaporate to an oily product; 81%. DCC is only a dehydrating agent (no atoms in product).
General procedure 4.1.4: amine 1 (0.012 mol), anhydride (0.01 mol), Zn dust (0.010 g), glacial AcOH / CH2Cl2 (15 mL), reflux 4-5 h; poured into ice water, precipitate recrystallised from EtOH; 71%.

notes: 3 steps. Acid used for 2d is not named explicitly in the experimental ('substituted acid derivative'); 2-chlorobenzoic acid is inferred from the anhydride name 2d. 2,4-Diaminophenol is written as the free base (the paper uses the dihydrochloride; HCl is not a skeleton atom supplier). The paper's text calls 3g '4-ethylphenyl' but Scheme 1 gives 3g = 2-methylphenyl and 3h = 4-ethylphenyl (irrelevant to 3d). Anhydride uses only one acyl half; the other equivalent of acid is lost as 2-chlorobenzoic acid.
